content: 1. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of everolimus by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, close monitoring is required. 2. Nelfinavir decreases the effects of exenatide injectable solution and suspension through mechanisms related to insulin resistance. Reports indicate hyperglycemia due to protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Famotidine reduces the levels or effects of nelfinavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Conversely, nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of fedratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If fedratinib must be co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the fedratinib dose to 200 mg/day. 5. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of felbamate, felodipine, and fentanyl (including intranasal, transdermal, and transmucosal forms) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If fentanyl co-administration is necessary, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust the fentanyl dose as needed. 6. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of fesoterodine, fluticasone (inhaled, intranasal, and furoate forms), and flurazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. For flurazepam, consider lowering the benzodiazepine dose or using alternatives. 7. Nelfinavir increases the toxicity of fluvastatin by inhibiting OATP1B1 transporters, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Fluvoxamine increases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Fostamatinib increases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Nelfinavir also increases the levels or effects of fostamatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to R406 (fostamatinib’s active metabolite). Monitor for toxicities and consider dose reduction. 11. Garlic decreases nelfinavir levels through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Grapefruit increases nelfinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of gefitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of gefitinib-related adverse effects. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 14. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of guanfacine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly increase guanfacine plasma concentrations. For extended-release guanfacine, reduce the dose to half the recommended amount. Specific recommendations for immediate-release guanfacine are not available. Monitor closely. 15. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of haloperidol and hydrocodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 16. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of hydrocortisone and hydroxyprogesterone caproate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of ibrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If short-term use of a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is necessary, interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the inhibitor is discontinued. 18. Ibuprofen/famotidine decreases nelfinavir levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of idelalisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administered, monitor for signs of idelalisib toxicity and adjust the dosage as needed. Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor and may increase the risk of adverse effects when combined with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 20. Nelfinavir decreases the levels or effects of ifosfamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP2B6 inhibitors may reduce ifosfamide’s therapeutic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of iloperidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may increase plasma levels of drugs eliminated by CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely.
